web_evidence.title: The Wrong Side Of Goodbye Excerpt
web_evidence.note: The author’s official sustained excerpt covers chapters 1 and 2 and consistently narrates Bosch externally as “he,” while freely reporting his perceptions, memories, and thoughts.

web_evidence.title: The Wrong Side of Goodbye review: One of US crime fiction’s great detectives
web_evidence.note: This reputable review reproduces third-person Bosch narration from the novel’s climax, corroborating that the third-person mode continues well beyond the opening.

search_log: Searched the verified title and author with “excerpt” and “first chapter”; found and opened Michael Connelly’s authorized multi-chapter excerpt.

Searched the title with “point of view,” “third person,” “narrator,” and “third-person narration”; results included an explicit user review, general reviews, and audiobook-narrator pages, but most were not independently diagnostic of grammatical narrative person.
Opened the Google Books record and preview metadata; its publisher synopsis and common-term index were useful for title verification but not used as person evidence.

Searched for alternating point of view, multiple narrators, epistolary form, diaries, and frame narrative; results described two alternating investigations or the audiobook performer, not sustained narration in different grammatical persons, and revealed no credible contrary structure.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person, centered closely on Harry Bosch. Multiple interior Goodreads passages sustain external “Bosch/he” narration with access to his perceptions and thoughts, and the author-authorized opening independently shows the same mode across two chapters. The Irish Times supplies corroborating third-person prose from near the climax. First- and second-person forms in the quote set occur only in dialogue or generic maxims, not autonomous narrative sections. Searches found no credible evidence of first-person, second-person, epistolary, framed, or person-alternating base narration; the only material limitation is that the strongest authorized web excerpt covers the opening rather than the entire book.
